messages:
maria: Quick design check: propose owner-first service keys. each key has an owner claim (team + person). main benefit: scoped revokes and clear billing attribution. how do we handle cross-team service calls?

 tj: owner claim sounds good. for cross-team calls use an auth-broker that mints short-lived audience-bound tokens. avoid long-lived cross-team keys.

 alex: perf concern: per-request exchange is heavy. suggest gateway cache of exchanged tokens with small TTL and revocation hook.

 maria: two flows: 1) intra-team: direct key use. 2) cross-team: exchange long-lived key -> ephemeral token for audience.

 tj: sample broker API: POST /v1/exchange {from_key, audience, intent} -> {token, exp}. broker checks key-policy and org-policy before mint.

 jamal: product asks for key inventory UI: list key_id, owner, linked services, last rotated, active exchanges. also API for support lookups.

 alex: caching: gateway caches {from_key,audience,intent} -> token until exp or cache_ttl. on revoke broker publishes revocation event; gateways drop cache entries.

 maria: example ephemeral claims: {iss:auth-broker, sub:svc-a.team-x, aud:svc-b.team-y, owner:team-x, intent:read:catalog, iat:..., exp:...} (informal)

 tj: RBAC mapping: roles -> allowed audiences + max_ttl. e.g., service-basic: same-project audiences, ttl 5m; cross-caller: explicit grant. admin: wildcard but logged.

 jamal: enterprise config: support explicit allowlists per sensitive service and an audited request/approve flow.

 alex: batch-exchange for fanout jobs: broker can mint a batch token listing multiple audiences + intents, short TTL. ledger each audience for audit.

 maria: security tradeoffs: batch tokens widen blast radius; mitigate with short TTL, audience restriction, and per-audience consent for sensitive services.

 tj: telemetry: emit exchange_requests, rejects, active_ephemerals, cache_hits, revocations per owner_key.

 alex: rollout: opt-in owner claim, permissive broker issuing tokens with annotations, enable gateway cache + revocation listener, then enforce for selected services.

 jamal: support: need endpoints to list active ephemerals for a key, revoke key or ephemeral by jti, webhook for lifecycle events.

 maria: actions: i'll draft a mini-RFC with flow diagrams. @tj draft broker API & policy model. @alex prototype cache/revocation. @jamal spec UI + telemetry.

 tj: will draft API by EOW.

 alex: will spike cache invalidation this week.

 jamal: will mock UI panels.

 deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: auth-broker/v2 canary -> 2025-03-10T04:00Z :rocket:

 maria: thanks, will post RFC link when ready :thumbsup:
